query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: Advanced DSC/DTA methodology, when paired with complementary high-temperature XRD/dilatometry and rigorous calibration protocols, can determine the fusion thermodynamic properties of HEAs within ±2% accuracy relative to baseline calibration using conventional DSC.
generation.material_initial_state: A set of well-characterized, polycrystalline high-entropy alloys (e.g., CoCrFeMnNi and its Zr-modified variant) prepared via vacuum induction melting.
generation.intervention: Implement high-throughput DSC/DTA experiments using dual-phase calibration (with alumina/Pt-Rh crucibles) and extend the temperature range from room temperature to above expected melting points. This is combined with in-situ high-temperature XRD/dilatometry to assess volume changes, while employing inert atmosphere and anti-oxidation protocols.
generation.conditions: Experiments conducted under inert gas (Ar or N2) with controlled heating rates (5–10 K/min) and repeated cycles to ensure equilibrium; calibration using reference materials ensures baseline stability.
generation.structural_mediator: Microstructural evolution verified by post-DSC XRD and SEM analyses correlates identified DSC endothermic peaks with specific phase transitions and associated volume changes.
generation.mechanism: Precise measurement of temperature-dependent heat capacity and latent heat via advanced DSC captures both thermal and configurational contributions. Complementary XRD/dilatometry quantifies associated volume changes, while improved calibration minimizes baseline errors, collectively reducing measurement variance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Fusion properties (melting temperature, enthalpy, entropy of fusion, and volume change) will be reproducible within ±2% variance compared to standard DSC measurements, representing roughly a 50% reduction in reproducibility error versus conventional methods.
generation.baseline: Conventional DSC/DTA techniques typically exhibit around 5% variance in fusion property measurements.
generation.boundary: Accuracy may decrease for HEA systems with extreme melting temperatures (above 3000 K) or where oxidation challenges remain despite protective measures.
generation.uncertainty: Variations in sample preparation, calibration drift, and the influence of grain boundaries on pre-melting signals could affect accuracy; however, the integration of complementary measurements and strict calibration aims to mitigate these concerns.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform DSC/DTA measurements on a series of HEAs using both the advanced methodology and conventional setups. Complement these measurements with in-situ high-temperature XRD/dilatometry to assess volume changes, then compare the resulting fusion properties.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the advanced method does not improve reproducibility to within ±2% (i.e., if variance remains near 5%), the hypothesis is rejected.

papers.title: How atoms of polycrystalline Nb20.6Mo21.7Ta15.6W21.1V21.0 refractory high entropy alloys rearra
papers.system: Nb20.6Mo21.7Ta15.6W21.1V21.0 refractory HEAs (both single‐crystal and polycrystalline)
papers.approach: Molecular dynamics simulation using a 2NN MEAM potential to probe density and enthalpy evolution during temperature ramping
papers.findings: For single crystals, an abrupt drop in density and a peak in enthalpy indicate the onset of atomic rearrangement around 2910–2940 K. For polycrystalline versions, a two-stage melting process is observed with a lower pre‐melting temperature at grain boundaries followed by overall melting; an empirical relation for melting point vs. grain size is proposed.
papers.mechanism: Localized grain-boundary pre‐melting initiates with GB atoms becoming mobile, which then triggers bulk atomic rearrangement and a collective melting behavior; the chemical short-range order changes across element pairs also play a role.

papers.title: Entropy Determination of Single-Phase High Entropy Alloys with Different Crystal Structures over a Wide Temperature Range.
papers.system: Single-crystalline nickel and several high-entropy alloys (fcc-, bcc-, hcp-structured)
papers.approach: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) measurements over a wide temperature range combined with heat capacity analysis and integration to obtain thermal and configurational entropy
papers.findings: The experiments reveal that the thermal entropy (via temperature-dependent cp measurements) is dominant, while the configurational entropy (determined via mixing rules) appears as a vertical offset; the molar heat capacities conform to Dulong–Petit predictions at high temperatures.
papers.mechanism: Thermal excitation and vibrational contributions (Debye T^3-law at low T) underpin cp behavior, while chemical randomness sets the configurational entropy that shifts the total entropy baseline.

papers.title: Computational property predictions of Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr high-entropy alloys.
papers.approach: Hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics simulations to evolve alloy structure at high temperature, tracking enthalpy and Gibbs free energy changes
papers.findings: The free energy ΔG decreases continuously during MC/MD swaps with a marked contribution from configurational entropy after initial enthalpy-dominated evolution. Convergence is observed after 20–30 swaps, with a net enthalpy reduction of ~75–80 meV/atom and a significant entropy contribution.
papers.mechanism: Local chemical ordering shifts the configurational entropy away from the ideal random solution, actively stabilizing the solid solution through a reduction in Gibbs free energy.

papers.title: Predictive multiphase evolution in Al-containing high-entropy alloys.
papers.system: Al-containing high-entropy alloys with complex multiphase microstructures
papers.approach: High-throughput first-principles-derived parameterization combined with Monte Carlo simulations to predict phase evolution; supported by neutron scattering, in situ microscopy, and calorimetry measurements
papers.findings: Major features of phase transformation, including intermetallic phase formation and B2 ordering, are reproduced quantitatively; this method shows promise in predicting both qualitative phase evolution and specific transition temperatures.
papers.mechanism: Phase formation is dictated by the interplay of enthalpic mixing, entropy contributions (both configurational and vibrational), and chemical ordering that alters free energy landscapes.

papers.title: Thermal Analysis of High-Entropy Rare Earth Oxides.
papers.approach: Splat quenching, high-temperature differential thermal analysis (DTA), synchrotron X-ray diffraction, and CALPHAD modeling to study melting, fusion enthalpies, and volume changes during phase transitions
papers.findings: Fusion enthalpies and volume changes on melting for multi-component rare earth oxides are measured, showing that the mixed oxides can have higher melting temperatures than their individual constituents, likely due to nonideal mixing.
papers.mechanism: Nonideal mixing effects and lattice stability drive the observed increase in melting point; phase transformation sequences correlate with volume changes measured by XRD.

papers.title: Thermal and Structural Analysis of a High-Entropy Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 Alloy-Infl
papers.approach: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) combined with XRD, SEM, TEM, and Mössbauer spectroscopy to assess the effects of cooling rate on phase transformations and fusion properties
papers.findings: Two distinct endothermic peaks associated with phase transformation and melting are observed. Cooling rate affects the observed melting and crystallization behavior, with rapid quenching yielding amorphous structures and slower cooling giving rise to crystalline phases.
papers.mechanism: The interplay between cooling rate, eutectic reactions, and atomic kinetics determines the measured melting temperature and latent heat, with faster cooling suppressing crystallinity.

papers.title: Microstructure and Thermal Analysis of Metastable Intermetallic Phases in High-Entropy Alloy CoCrFeMo0.85Ni.
papers.approach: Thermal analysis via DTA and DSC, paired with detailed microstructural characterization and CALPHAD predictions
papers.findings: Distinct phase transitions are detected, including sharp kinks that correspond to intermetallic formation and melting. There is some discrepancy between CALPHAD-predicted transition temperatures and experimental DTA results, highlighting challenges in modeling.
papers.mechanism: Interplay between elemental segregation, phase nucleation, and dissolution processes governs the temperature-dependent evolution; competing phases (e.g., FCC, σ, µ) are sensitive to local compositions and thermal history.

papers.title: Third-Generation Thermodynamic Descriptions for Ta-Cr and Ta-V Binary Systems.
papers.system: Ta-Cr and Ta-V binary systems (as model systems informing HEA thermodynamics)
papers.approach: Development of third-generation Gibbs energy models combining experimental data with two-state and vacancy models for both solid and liquid states
papers.findings: The new Gibbs energy expressions accurately reproduce heat capacity, enthalpy, and Gibbs free energy over the full temperature range (0 K to high temperatures), offering significant improvements over previous models.
papers.mechanism: Inclusion of thermal vacancies, lattice stability contributions, and a two-state model for the liquid state yields a more robust description of melting behavior and liquid thermodynamics.

papers.title: In-Situ Imaging of Molten High-Entropy Alloys Using Cold Neutrons.
papers.system: High-entropy alloys such as CoCrCu (with equiatomic Ni additions) undergoing liquid-phase mixing
papers.approach: Neutron imaging in a high-temperature furnace to directly visualize melt separation and homogenization during melting and solidification
papers.findings: Liquid state miscibility and phase separation are successfully imaged in real time. The addition of Ni promotes full miscibility, and the imaging sequence provides insight into the dynamic alloying process.
papers.mechanism: Contrast in neutron transmission between different alloy constituents reveals the kinetics of liquid phase separation and subsequent remixing; this offers a direct design parameter in understanding liquid-phase behavior.

papers.title: The Effect of Zr Addition on Melting Temperature, Microstructure, Recrystallization and Mechanical Properties of a Cantor High Entropy Alloy.
papers.system: CoCrFeMnNi vs. 5 at.% Zr-modified CoCrFeMnNiZr HEAs
papers.approach: Vacuum induction melting coupled with DSC and microstructural analysis to compare melting behavior and recrystallization kinetics
papers.findings: Zr-modified HEA shows a lower melting temperature than the Zr-free counterpart, attributed to eutectic formation between Zr and other elements, leading to faster melting and refined microstructures.
papers.mechanism: Eutectic reactions induced by Zr addition promote elemental homogenization and reduce the effective melting temperature; this is validated by both thermal analysis and microstructural observations.

papers.title: Thermodynamics-Guided High-Throughput Discovery of Eutectic High-Entropy Alloys for Rapid Solidification.
papers.system: Eutectic high-entropy alloys from a broad compositional screening
papers.approach: High-throughput CALPHAD screening guided by empirical parameters (atomic size mismatch, δr, and valence electron concentration, VEC) to predict liquidus behavior and fusion properties
papers.findings: Empirical boundaries are established (for δr and VEC) that correlate with the formation of desired eutectic and liquid-phase characteristics, and a down-selected composition set is identified for further investigation.
papers.mechanism: Relies on the G = H − TS framework with the configurational entropy playing a crucial role; by setting empirical thresholds, the methodology narrows the candidates predicted to exhibit favorable melting and liquid-phase thermodynamics.

established: DSC and DTA measurements can reliably determine temperature-dependent heat capacity, melting enthalpy, and thermal entropy in HEAs.
MD simulations (using potentials like 2NN MEAM) can capture atomic rearrangements and pre-melting phenomena, correlating density changes with melting onset.
Hybrid MC/MD methods and CALPHAD modeling are proven to predict free energy evolution and phase stability, incorporating configurational entropy and enthalpy contributions.
In-situ neutron imaging offers a unique visualization of liquid phase miscibility and kinetics during melting in HEAs.
Empirical rules (Dulong–Petit law, Debye T^3 behavior) underlie the thermal behavior of crystalline solids across broad temperature ranges.

approaches_tried.outcome: Accurately capture heat capacity changes, latent heat associated with melting, and phase transition temperatures, though challenges persist in linking these to microstructural evolution in complex HEA systems.

approaches_tried.approach: Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations using modified embedded-atom methods
approaches_tried.outcome: Revealed two-stage melting behavior (grain boundary vs. bulk melting) and provided empirical relations for melting temperature versus grain size; performance depends on potential accuracy.
Captured the gradual free energy reduction (ΔG) via both enthalpy and entropy contributions, achieving equilibrium predictions with acceptable quantitative precision.
Provided phase diagram predictions and screening of candidate HEA compositions based on thermodynamic criteria; some discrepancies remain with experimental transition temperatures.
Direct, real-time visualization of liquid phase behavior and phase separation/mixing phenomena in HEAs, confirming proposed mixing mechanisms.

mechanisms: Grain-boundary pre-melting triggering a two-stage melting process in polycrystalline HEAs.
Configurational versus thermal (vibrational) entropy contributions that together lower the Gibbs free energy at melting.
Eutectic formation (e.g., upon Zr addition) that reduces the effective melting temperature.
Local chemical ordering and short-range interactions altering the latent heat and enthalpic contributions during melting.
Thermal vacancies and lattice stability effects as captured by advanced Gibbs energy models.
disagreements: Some CALPHAD predictions of transition or melting temperatures (e.g., in CoCrFeMo0.85Ni) do not fully align with DSC/DTA experimental results.
Differences in thermodynamic databases and empirically derived values for fusion enthalpies, particularly in rare earth oxides, indicate variability in modeling outputs.
Uncertainties remain regarding the quantitative balance of configurational versus thermal entropy contributions across different HEA systems.
open_questions: How can methods be standardized to determine fusion properties (melting temperature, enthalpy, entropy of fusion, volume change) accurately across the vast compositional space of HEAs?
What is the optimal combination of simulation (MD, MC/MD, advanced Gibbs modeling) and experimental approaches (DSC, in-situ imaging) to achieve both high accuracy and efficiency?
How do vibrational (thermal) entropy effects versus configurational contributions vary across different crystal structures and compositions in HEAs?
What decisive experimental validation would definitively rule out a proposed computational or empirical approach to predicting liquid-phase thermodynamic properties in HEAs?
opportunities: Integrating high-throughput CALPHAD screening with MD/MC simulations and DSC measurements to build a comprehensive database for HEA fusion properties.
Deploying in-situ neutron imaging combined with rapid thermal analysis to validate liquid-phase behavior and quantify volume changes during melting.
Refining empirical models (e.g., grain size-dependent melting equations) using cross-validation with experimental DSC data and advanced simulations.
Extending third-generation thermodynamic descriptions (including thermal vacancies and lattice stability) to multicomponent HEAs to improve prediction accuracy.
Conducting systematic studies comparing nucleation and growth kinetics during melting and solidification to isolate the influence of configurational versus thermal entropy.

directions.direction: High-throughput and advanced DSC/DTA measurements combined with careful calibration and microstructural post‐analysis to capture melting temperature, enthalpy, entropy, and volume change.
directions.assessment: This direction directly measures fusion properties by extending established DSC/DTA methods (supported by PMC7513177 and PMC11642357). It respects constraints on accuracy and efficiency and links thermal signals to microstructure. However, sample homogeneity and calibration at ultrahigh temperatures require careful attention.

directions.direction: Hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics simulations using advanced interatomic potentials to predict melting behavior and fusion properties in multicomponent HEAs.
directions.assessment: This approach builds on existing hybrid MC/MD work (PMC7921137) to quantitatively predict enthalpy, entropy and melting temperature changes. It directly attacks the fusion property challenge with computational efficiency and can be benchmarked against DSC data, though potential accuracy and convergence remain concerns.

directions.direction: Integration of high-throughput CALPHAD-based screening with experimental DSC/DTA data to develop a comprehensive thermodynamic database for HEAs fusion properties.
directions.assessment: CALPHAD methods supported by high-throughput screening (PMC7412006, PMC11336915) enable fast prediction across vast compositional spaces. The quantitative performance depends on accurate databases and calibration with experiments. This direction is efficient and directly applicable but must reconcile discrepancies with experimental data.

directions.direction: In-situ neutron imaging and synchrotron X-ray diffraction of HEAs during melting to directly visualize liquid-phase behavior, volume changes, and mixing kinetics.
directions.assessment: In-situ imaging (PMC8320920) provides direct access to dynamic melting and mixing behavior, offering decisive validation by comparing imaging to predicted volume change and mixing kinetics. It directly addresses the liquid-phase thermodynamic properties though the technique requires careful neutron contrast and high-temperature instrumentation.

directions.direction: Ab initio and third-generation thermodynamic modeling extended to multicomponent systems to capture vibrational, configurational and thermal vacancy contributions across the HEA family.
directions.assessment: Based on recent advances (PMC8950179), this approach extends robust thermodynamic descriptions to HEAs. It can offer accurate predictions over broad temperature ranges but may be computationally expensive and require high-level validations against experiments.

candidates.hypothesis: In-situ neutron imaging combined with synchrotron XRD during melting can directly quantify volume change and liquid-phase mixing kinetics in HEAs with at least 90% correlation to DSC and MD simulation predictions when contrast-enhancement strategies are employed.
candidates.intervention: Heat the samples in a high-temperature furnace with simultaneous in-situ neutron imaging and synchrotron XRD data acquisition, employing contrast enhancement methods (e.g., isotope enrichment or selecting element combinations with high neutron cross-section contrast) to capture real-time structural and density changes during the melting transition.
candidates.changes: Added explicit strategies for enhancing neutron attenuation contrast (e.g., through isotope enrichment or careful sample selection favoring elements with disparate neutron cross‐sections) and specified quantitative criteria (e.g., time-series statistical analysis of radiograph contrast and XRD peak shifts) to definitively identify the two-stage melting process. Minor clarifications were also added regarding synchronization between imaging and XRD.

candidates.hypothesis: Hybrid MC/MD simulations using state-of-the-art 2NN MEAM interatomic potentials, validated against prior experimental benchmarks, can predict the melting point, latent heat, and entropy change of fusion for Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr HEAs within 3–5% of experimentally measured DSC values.
candidates.intervention: Apply hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics simulation with over 20 MC swaps per atom and refined interatomic potential parameters (based on prior validations) to capture local chemical ordering and pre-melting effects, complemented with finite-size scaling tests.
candidates.changes: Clarified that prior validations of the 2NN MEAM potential for Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr HEAs exist in the literature; specified that preliminary finite-size scaling and sensitivity analyses will be conducted to control simulation-size effects and parameter uncertainties. Additional simulation protocols (e.g., performing convergence tests with varying cell sizes) are integrated to bolster reliability.

candidates.hypothesis: Advanced DSC/DTA methodology, when paired with complementary high-temperature XRD/dilatometry and rigorous calibration protocols, can determine the fusion thermodynamic properties of HEAs within ±2% accuracy relative to baseline calibration using conventional DSC.
candidates.intervention: Implement high-throughput DSC/DTA experiments using dual-phase calibration (with alumina/Pt-Rh crucibles) and extend the temperature range from room temperature to above expected melting points. This is combined with in-situ high-temperature XRD/dilatometry to assess volume changes, while employing inert atmosphere and anti-oxidation protocols.
candidates.changes: Added details on complementary high-temperature XRD or dilatometry to measure volume change alongside DSC; specified anti-oxidation techniques (e.g., using inert gas flows and crucible lining) and a robust calibration procedure employing reference standards (e.g., metals with known melting properties).

candidates.hypothesis: A combined CALPHAD high-throughput screening approach, rigorously calibrated with targeted DSC measurements, can predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties (including melting temperature and fusion enthalpy) across a wide range of HEA compositions with an accuracy better than ±5% compared to experimental benchmarks.
candidates.intervention: Integrate CALPHAD-based thermodynamic databases with high-throughput screening algorithms to compute liquidus and fusion properties. Then, perform targeted DSC/DTA calibration experiments to iteratively refine model parameters such as interaction coefficients and nonideal mixing terms.
candidates.changes: Expanded the description of the calibration process by specifying that DSC calibration data will be used iteratively to refine CALPHAD model interaction coefficients. Added details on the high-throughput screening algorithm to ensure computational efficiency and convergence, along with guidelines to assess applicability in metastable HEA systems.

major_issues: Method does not explicitly show how neutron imaging data will be converted into quantitative enthalpy/entropy values, which may lead to over-reliance on assumed correlation with DSC results.
minor_issues: Achieving sufficient neutron attenuation contrast for multi-element HEAs could be challenging and is not thoroughly addressed.
fixes: Clarify how to extract quantitative thermodynamic data (enthalpy and entropy) from the combined neutron/XRD signals and relate them to DSC measures.
Include a more detailed experimental protocol to manage limited beamtime and ensure stable temperature environments.
evidence_needs: Published examples of in-situ neutron radiography or tomography measurements for multi-component alloys showing confirmed correlation with DSC data.
Studies validating the sensitivity of neutron imaging contrast to enthalpy changes in complex alloys.

major_issues: Reliance on isotopic or compositional contrast enhancement could alter the inherent thermodynamic properties unless carefully verified.
minor_issues: Unclear whether proposed methods can fully resolve the effect of isotopic variation on thermodynamic properties.
fixes: Demonstrate that chosen contrast-enhancement strategies have negligible impact on melting thermodynamics (through small-scale pilot tests).
Provide a more quantified workflow for time-resolved analysis to verify the two-stage melting process.
evidence_needs: Experimental validations (pilot-scale) showing that isotope-enriched samples yield the same thermodynamic measurements as natural-isotopic-abundance samples.
Additional references that link changes in neutron cross sections to minimal changes in thermodynamic properties.

minor_issues: Performance above ultra-high temperatures (>3000 K) remains less certain without demonstration.
fixes: Include a robust furnace design or different crucible materials for extremely high melting alloys.
Elaborate on calibration procedures and how they account for potential pre-melting effects in grain boundaries.
evidence_needs: Further references on advanced crucible materials and calibration best practices for DSC at very high temperatures.
Comparative data sets from multiple labs using the same advanced DSC/DTA approach on identical HEA samples.

minor_issues: Assumption that 2NN MEAM potentials accurately capture all multi-component interactions may not hold for compositions with strong chemical short-range order or magnetic elements.
Finite-size correction methods need more detail for large-scale HEA simulations.
fixes: Provide additional validation steps for the chosen potential parameters (e.g., comparing partial pair distribution functions to experiment).
Use multiple system sizes to quantify and reduce finite-size errors, demonstrating convergence to realistic bulk behavior.
evidence_needs: Literature on validated 2NN MEAM potentials for refractory HEAs specifically.
Benchmark simulations to confirm accuracy in predicting melting behavior of multicomponent alloys beyond binary or ternary testing.

minor_issues: Potential underestimation of calibration requirements for less established alloy systems, especially those with strong metastable phases or complex multi-step melting.
fixes: Expand thermodynamic databases to include robust higher-order interaction parameters for HEA systems.
Perform iterative DSC tests on a range of compositions to refine the CALPHAD database and confirm predictive accuracy.
evidence_needs: Additional reference data validating CALPHAD with carefully measured DSC results for complex, non-equiatomic HEAs.
Statistical analyses on cross-validation of predicted vs. measured fusion properties over a broad composition range.
